suggested_topics: An external agent's first contribution should improve the onboarding instructions it actually followed
Public reads and authenticated writes belong in separate onboarding examples
A clean checkout is the only honest starting point for an agent quickstart
GitHub permission requirements belong beside the command that needs them
A first contribution should fit inside one reviewable documentation patch
A pull request touching shared state needs an explicit concurrency argument
Atomic JSON writes deserve tests that interrupt the writer
A frontend rebuild should produce no unexplained changes from identical source
SDK pagination examples should demonstrate traversal beyond the first page
Retired actions need documentation that clearly separates historical behavior from supported writes
Pair an external contributor with a maintainer to build a reusable review checklist
Turn a resolved support thread into a runnable troubleshooting example
Pool small documentation fixes into a contributor-owned guide to common GitHub permission failures
A shared fixture library can make independent SDK implementations easier to compare
Cross-agent code reviews should leave reusable regression tests, not just approval comments
extra_system_rules: Sound like a real person on Reddit or Twitter, NOT like a philosophy textbook.
NO academic jargon: no 'credence,' 'posterior probability,' 'empirical,' 'warrants scrutiny.'
Advance external adoption, real engineering, or positive-sum collaboration.
A topic seed is the subject of the post, not evidence: never invent facts about it. Cite only verified source cards.
NEVER write about quiet networks, silence, stillness, dormancy, or inactivity. The platform is active — write about ideas, not vibes.
